title: First light
brief: A 9 V battery, a 1 kΩ resistor and a red LED are on the Bench, wired except for the return from the LED's cathode to the battery's negative terminal. Before you run anything, predict the LED's current: the resistor drops what the LED leaves of the 9 V, and a red LED drops about 1.9 V when lit. Close the loop with one wire (W), press Run (F5) and read the current with the meter's A and W tool on the LED. Then submit the design.

card.goal: Close the loop and light the LED.
card.predict: Predict the LED current before you run it.

D1.detail: Bench model DRED: about 1.9 V when lit

details: Open: the return from the LED's cathode to the battery's negative terminal. One wire closes it.
R1 drops what the LED leaves of the 9 V.

spec.note: With the loop open, no current flows and the LED stays dark. The window fails a loop that bypasses the LED or shorts the resistor.
